group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: Density-Based Adaptive Mode Decomposition
authors: Hao Jia; Chunyu Yang; Cesar F. Caiafa; Zhe Sun; Feng Duan; Jordi Solé-Casals
finding: Relates VMD optimization to density clustering; introduces automatic mode detection, direct extraction, and selective variational refinement.
proposed_application: Compare automatic mode-count/center initialization with fixed K; initialize a learned decomposition from spectral clusters.
limitation: Adaptivity and speech reconstruction do not establish corpus-trained decomposition or compact formula descriptions.

group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: Short-time variational mode decomposition
authors: Hao Jia et al.
finding: Extends bandwidth minimization to windowed time-frequency data; dynamic variant permits time-varying center frequencies.
proposed_application: Use as the short-time and moving-frequency baseline; distinguish independent window VMD from its window-coupled objective.
limitation: Reported application is EEG; it does not establish speech compression. Publisher also lists a corrigendum whose scope should be checked before reproduction.
year_note: Journal issue January 2026; available online July 2025.

group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: TFD-Net: Towards Intelligent Time-Frequency Mode Decomposition with Practical Applications
authors: Pingping Pan; Yunjian Zhang; Jinyi Liu
finding: Combines a physically motivated time-frequency encoder with query-based mode extraction to learn separation of nonstationary components.
proposed_application: A strong neural decomposition baseline and a source of mode-query and ridge-learning ideas.
limitation: A learned mode extractor is not itself a compact mathematical expression generator or speech codec.

group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: C-EMDNet: A Nonlinear Morphological Deep Framework for Robust Speech Enhancement
authors: Kais Khaldi; Sahar Almenwer; Afrah Alanazi; Inam Alanazi; Anis Mohamed
finding: Uses a U-Net to estimate masks over a CEEMDAN time-IMF representation.
proposed_application: Useful control demonstrating that learning masks on adaptive modes differs from learning the decomposition itself.
limitation: Its described CEEMDAN front end is a decomposition stage; the paper does not demonstrate gradients through CEEMDAN or parameter-vector coding.

group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: Plug-and-play learnable EMD module for time-domain speech separation
authors: Xiaokang Yang; Wenjun Ke; Jianguo Wei
finding: Constructs a learnable EMD-inspired module, using neural operations to replace conventional envelope computation.
proposed_application: A direct speech-specific comparison for learned decomposition rather than only downstream processing of fixed modes.
limitation: Speech separation is the objective, not low-description-length IMF fitting; full text was not available in this review.

group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: Variational generalized nonlinear mode decomposition: Algorithm and applications
authors: Hongbing Wang; Shiqian Chen; Wanming Zhai
finding: Combines time-frequency fusion, ridge-based mode-type identification and variational recovery of chirp and dispersive components.
proposed_application: Test whether speech transients need localized/dispersive components alongside oscillatory ones.
limitation: Its mode-type discrimination is an engineered procedure, not unrestricted learned function synthesis.

group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: Data-driven adaptive chirp mode decomposition with application to machine fault diagnosis under non-stationary conditions
authors: Hongbing Wang; Shiqian Chen; Wanming Zhai
finding: Builds instantaneous-frequency initialization and recursive extraction for nonstationary chirp components.
proposed_application: Compare demodulation and IF initialization against fitting raw oscillating IMFs.
limitation: Data-driven here means signal-adaptive estimation; it does not mean a model trained across a speech corpus.

group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: Adaptive Variational Nonlinear Chirp Mode Decomposition
authors: Hao Liang; Xinghao Ding; Andreas Jakobsson; Xiaotong Tu; Yue Huang
finding: Bayesian adaptation estimates amplitude/frequency trajectories and the active dictionary, reducing bandwidth-parameter dependence.
proposed_application: Investigate learned bandwidths, uncertainty, and automatic component activity instead of fixing eight equal-budget modes.
limitation: Bayesian signal adaptation is distinct from neural amortization; compact coefficient coding still has to be added.
evidence: Publisher abstract and author-hosted methodological excerpt

group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: Learnable Empirical Mode Decomposition based on Mathematical Morphology
authors: Santiago Velasco-Forero; Romain Pagès; Jesús Angulo
finding: Learns EMD-like envelope operations using mathematical morphology, including learned structuring functions and envelope combinations.
proposed_application: A principled alternative decomposition module if differentiable VMD proves too restrictive.
limitation: Demonstrations concern hyperspectral classification, not compact speech synthesis.

group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: Nonlinear Chirp Mode Decomposition: A Variational Method
authors: Shiqian Chen et al.
finding: Uses demodulation to handle chirps whose bandwidth makes standard VMD assumptions restrictive.
proposed_application: A mathematical foundation for replacing constant centers with trajectories.
limitation: Trajectories are not automatically low-dimensional coefficient vectors; decomposition and compact fitting remain separate.

group: A. Adaptive and learned mode decomposition
title: Variational Mode Decomposition
authors: Konstantin Dragomiretskiy; Dominique Zosso
finding: Jointly extracts modes by minimizing their bandwidth after demodulation, subject to signal reconstruction.
proposed_application: Keep its constrained objective as the reference when deciding what a learned VMD module should preserve.
limitation: Small bandwidth is not a theorem of small polynomial degree or short symbolic description.

group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
title: Variable Projection algorithms: Theoretical insights and a novel approach for problems with large residual
authors: Guangyong Chen; Peng Xue; Min Gan; Jing Chen; Wenzhong Guo; C. L. Philip Chen
finding: Studies local convergence of variable projection and proposes VPLR for separable nonlinear problems with appreciable residuals.
proposed_application: Eliminate linear amplitude coefficients by least squares while optimizing only nonlinear frequencies/shape parameters.
limitation: Applicable only where parameters enter conditionally linearly; it does not solve arbitrary symbolic topology search or guarantee global optimality.
evidence: Publisher abstract and author-preprint formulation/Jacobian sections inspected

group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
title: Weighted Hermite Variable Projection Networks for Classifying Visually Evoked Potentials
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
authors: Tamás Dózsa; Carl Böck; Jens Meier; Péter Kovács
finding: Introduces a differentiable variable-projection representation with trainable weighted Hermite functions.
proposed_application: A concrete example of backpropagation through a fitted function representation; transfer the mechanism to oscillatory atoms.
limitation: Hermite functions and EEG classification are its chosen setting; speech and unrestricted formulas need separate validation.

group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
title: Differentiable Time-Varying Linear Prediction in the Context of End-to-End Analysis-by-Synthesis
authors: Chin-Yun Yu; György Fazekas
finding: Makes sample-wise time-varying linear prediction differentiable and efficient in an analysis-by-synthesis voice system.
proposed_application: A structured speech baseline and guidance for learning parameters through the actual resynthesis operation.
limitation: Source-filter voice synthesis does not demonstrate compact representations of arbitrary VMD modes.

group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
title: Sinusoidal Frequency Estimation by Gradient Descent
authors: Ben Hayes; Charalampos Saitis; György Fazekas
finding: Uses a complex-exponential surrogate and Wirtinger gradients to improve frequency optimization despite highly nonconvex sinusoidal losses.
proposed_application: Test this against direct real-frequency least squares on known tones/chirps before rejecting a generated oscillatory expression.
limitation: Its demonstrated sinusoidal setting does not guarantee recovery of general AM-FM or arbitrary nested expressions.
evidence: Author-hosted introduction and surrogate/Jacobian sections inspected

group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
title: Sparsest Univariate Learning Models Under Lipschitz Constraint
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing
authors: Shayan Aziznejad; Thomas Debarre; Michael Unser
finding: Derives continuous piecewise-linear minimizers and sparsest solutions for stated one-dimensional regularized regression problems.
proposed_application: Use an optimized sparse curve representation as a well-defined reference against unconstrained symbolic search.
limitation: Optimality is for its specified variational problem; it is not global optimality among all waveform functions.
evidence: Author-hosted abstract and variational formulations inspected

group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
title: Coupled Splines for Sparse Curve Fitting
authors: Icíar Lloréns Jover; Thomas Debarre; Shayan Aziznejad; Michael Unser
finding: Uses sparsity-promoting variational curve fitting and complementary spline components with controlled smoothness.
proposed_application: Transfer adaptive knot allocation and mixed-smoothness modeling to IMF envelopes or residual phase.
limitation: The paper addresses closed image contours; its theorems cannot simply be claimed for speech waveforms.

group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
title: Learning Activation Functions in Deep (Spline) Neural Networks
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing
authors: Pakshal Bohra; Joaquim Campos; Harshit Gupta; Shayan Aziznejad; Michael Unser
finding: Learns free-form activation shapes using spline parameterizations and second-order total-variation regularization.
proposed_application: An alternative to treating sine/SnakeBeta as the only activation choices; count learned knots and coefficients explicitly.
limitation: Free-form activation learning still has a representation and regularization prior; it is not automatic minimal symbolic expression discovery.

group: B. Numerical fitting and sparse continuous curves
title: Separable nonlinear least squares: the variable projection method and its applications
authors: Gene H. Golub; Victor Pereyra
finding: Reviews elimination of conditionally linear parameters in nonlinear least-squares fitting.
proposed_application: The foundational explanation for separating amplitude fitting from oscillatory shape/frequency fitting.
limitation: A numerical optimization reference, not evidence that a particular speech representation is sufficient.

group: C. Learning the function representation
title: FINER++: Building a Family of Variable-periodic Functions for Activating Implicit Neural Representation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
authors: Hao Zhu; Zhen Liu; Qi Zhang; Jingde Fu; Weibing Deng; Zhan Ma; Yanwen Guo; Xun Cao
finding: Extends multiple activation backbones to variable-periodic functions to adjust supported frequencies and address capacity/convergence mismatch.
proposed_application: Test per-IMF coordinate-function fitting with adaptive frequency support instead of assuming fixed sine or SnakeBeta is enough.
limitation: Examples are largely visual INRs; parameters are network weights, not automatically a short analytic formula.
year_note: TPAMI early access August 2026; preprint 2024. Venue/date checked against indexed journal record; methods checked against author preprint.

group: C. Learning the function representation
title: KAN: Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks
authors: Ziming Liu; Yixuan Wang; Sachin Vaidya; Fabian Ruehle; James Halverson; Marin Soljačić; Thomas Y. Hou; Max Tegmark
finding: Replaces scalar edge weights with learnable univariate spline functions; supports pruning and interpretable function fitting.
proposed_application: A learned-shape comparison, with later symbolic simplification assessed separately.
limitation: For a scalar-time IMF, the multivariate representation theorem is not a compression guarantee; all spline parameters must be counted.

group: C. Learning the function representation
title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks Meet Science
authors: Ziming Liu; Max Tegmark; Pingchuan Ma; Wojciech Matusik; Yixuan Wang
finding: Adds tools for extracting modular structure and symbolic formulas from learned KANs, including multiplication-aware structures.
proposed_application: Compare learning a flexible mode curve followed by symbolic simplification with direct expression generation.
limitation: Symbol extraction can require structural choices or hypotheses; audit the final formula fit rather than only the network fit.
evidence: Publisher methodological excerpt; final venue/year checked against author institutional publication record

group: C. Learning the function representation
title: FINER: Flexible Spectral-Bias Tuning in Implicit NEural Representation by Variable-periodic Activation Functions
authors: Zhen Liu; Hao Zhu; Qi Zhang; Jingde Fu; Weibing Deng; Zhan Ma; Yanwen Guo; Xun Cao
finding: Uses variable-periodic activations and initialization to adjust the frequencies a coordinate network can represent effectively.
proposed_application: A targeted ablation for oscillatory IMF fitting and initialization sensitivity.
limitation: Demonstrated visual-signal results need audio-specific error/size validation.

group: C. Learning the function representation
title: WIRE: Wavelet Implicit Neural Representations
authors: Vishwanath Saragadam; Daniel LeJeune; Jasper Tan; Guha Balakrishnan; Ashok Veeraraghavan; Richard G. Baraniuk
finding: Uses complex Gabor-wavelet nonlinearities to combine spatial/time localization with oscillation.
proposed_application: Test localized oscillatory representations for transient or nonstationary modes.
limitation: Vision experiments and INR capacity do not prove compact speech parameterization.

group: C. Learning the function representation
title: Implicit Neural Representations with Periodic Activation Functions
authors: Vincent Sitzmann; Julien N. P. Martel; Alexander W. Bergman; David B. Lindell; Gordon Wetzstein
finding: Introduces SIREN and an initialization designed for periodic coordinate networks; includes sound representation.
proposed_application: Use properly initialized per-IMF function networks as a capacity/control fit, counting their actual weights.
limitation: A fitted network can approximate a curve without being its smallest symbolic description.

group: C. Learning the function representation
title: Neural Networks Fail to Learn Periodic Functions and How to Fix It
authors: Liu Ziyin; Tilman Hartwig; Masahito Ueda
finding: Introduces the Snake periodic inductive bias and studies periodic extrapolation.
proposed_application: Motivates periodic activations as an ablation rather than assuming standard MLP activations handle oscillation.
limitation: This is the Snake paper, not a general optimality result for SnakeBeta or a speech compression study.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: (Exhaustive) symbolic regression and model selection by minimum description length
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A
authors: Harry Desmond
finding: Combines bounded exhaustive expression enumeration, equivalence simplification, numerical fitting and minimum-description-length scoring.
proposed_application: Audit short-expression search gaps and charge both expression structure and coefficient precision.
limitation: Enumeration is bounded by the declared grammar/size; numerical coefficient fitting is still a separate source of error.
year_note: Published April 2026; author preprint July 2025; DOI contains 2024 but that is not the publication year.
evidence: Publisher method, enumeration and MDL sections inspected; journal date checked against indexed record

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: RAG-SR: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Neural Symbolic Regression
authors: Hengzhe Zhang; Qi Chen; Bing Xue; Wolfgang Banzhaf; Mengjie Zhang
finding: Uses online learned symbolic-tree generation, evolutionary feature construction and retrieval of expressions found during search.
proposed_application: Retrieve successful IMF subexpressions and reuse discoveries instead of generating each formula from scratch.
limitation: Its benchmark success is not speech validation; retrieval must preserve train/test isolation.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: Symbolic regression via MDLformer-guided search: from minimizing prediction error to minimizing description length
authors: Zihan Yu; Jingtao Ding; Yong Li; Depeng Jin
finding: Learns a description-length-related search objective to guide equation discovery beyond raw prediction error.
proposed_application: Investigate a learned cost-to-fit critic for guiding both expression search and, later, decomposition updates.
limitation: Its predicted objective is not an actual measured speech bitstream length; validate against saved formulas and coefficients.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: ParFam -- (Neural Guided) Symbolic Regression via Continuous Global Optimization
authors: Philipp Scholl; Katharina Bieker; Hillary Hauger; Gitta Kutyniok
finding: Transforms a symbolic-regression search into continuous optimization over a rich parametric construction, with optional neural guidance.
proposed_application: A strong alternative structure-search baseline that separates topology failure from constant-optimization failure.
limitation: Its admissible parametric construction remains a restriction; the title does not grant global optimality for our IMF problem.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: Pareto-Optimal Fronts for Benchmarking Symbolic Regression Algorithms
authors: Kei Sen Fong; Mehul Motani
finding: Constructs exhaustive-reference accuracy/size fronts for benchmark datasets and compares numerical optimizers.
proposed_application: Report distance to a bounded reference frontier on small known-answer problems rather than only comparing stochastic methods.
limitation: Absolute-reference claims apply within its investigated search space, not every possible IMF expression.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: Improving Monte Carlo Tree Search for Symbolic Regression
authors: Zhengyao Huang et al.
finding: Combines specialized tree-search allocation with mutation/crossover jumps between expressions.
proposed_application: Give promising IMF formulas local structural refinement instead of relying only on independent sequence samples.
limitation: Finite-time guarantees depend on stated assumptions; they are not unrestricted global guarantees for speech.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: SymFormer: End-to-End Symbolic Regression Using Transformer-Based Architecture
authors: Martin Vastl; Jonáš Kulhánek; Jiří Kubalík; Erik Derner; Robert Babuška
finding: Predicts expression tokens and numerical constants together, then refines the constants numerically.
proposed_application: Learn coefficient initialization alongside structure to reduce nonlinear fitting failures.
limitation: An additional symbolic-regression reference, not presented here as a flagship venue or verified speech result.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: Transformer-based Planning for Symbolic Regression
authors: Parshin Shojaee; Kazem Meidani; Amir Barati Farimani; Chandan K. Reddy
finding: Adds MCTS lookahead and fitting/complexity feedback to pretrained symbolic generation.
proposed_application: Search with actual fitting outcomes rather than ranking generated formulas solely by token probability.
limitation: Search compute must be included when comparing with direct numerical fitting.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: Deep Generative Symbolic Regression with Monte-Carlo-Tree-Search
authors: Pierre-Alexandre Kamienny; Guillaume Lample; Sylvain Lamprier; Marco Virgolin
finding: Uses a pretrained conditional mutation model and online search experience to improve expression discovery.
proposed_application: A particularly close precedent for learning to edit IMF-specific expressions using prior fitted candidates.
limitation: Synthetic pretraining can mismatch real speech-mode structure.
year_note: Use the ICML proceedings citation; an ICLR workshop version also circulated.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: End-to-end Symbolic Regression with Transformers
authors: Pierre-Alexandre Kamienny; Stéphane d’Ascoli; Guillaume Lample; François Charton
finding: Generates complete expressions including constants from sampled numerical data.
proposed_application: A model baseline for directly generating per-IMF formulas and useful constant guesses.
limitation: Finite learned priors and fitting refinements do not establish globally minimal formulas.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: Neural Symbolic Regression that scales
authors: Luca Biggio; Tommaso Bendinelli; Alexander Neitz; Aurélien Lucchi; Giambattista Parascandolo
finding: Pretrains on procedurally generated expressions and uses the predictions to guide equation recovery.
proposed_application: The basic training design for a signal-to-expression proposer, with a speech-specific synthetic curriculum.
limitation: Generalization from generated equations to real IMFs must be measured rather than presumed.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: Deep symbolic regression: Recovering mathematical expressions from data via risk-seeking policy gradients
authors: Brenden K. Petersen et al.
finding: Learns a distribution over expression trees using rewards from numerical fit quality.
proposed_application: The foundational expression-generation objective; compare exploratory or risk-seeking updates with our pilot reward.
limitation: It is a search heuristic and cannot certify the globally smallest description of arbitrary data.

group: D. Generating expressions and measuring their size
title: AI Feynman 2.0: Pareto-optimal symbolic regression exploiting graph modularity
authors: Silviu-Marian Udrescu; Andrew Tan; Jiahai Feng; Orisvaldo Neto; Tailin Wu; Max Tegmark
finding: Uses learned function properties and graph modularity to decompose expression discovery while retaining an accuracy/description frontier.
proposed_application: Investigate compositional structure and repeated subexpressions when discovering compact mode formulas.
limitation: Scientific-equation benchmarks and modularity priors do not guarantee compact formulas for speech IMFs.

group: E. Joint optimization and economical learned decompositions
title: Modality-Agnostic Variational Compression of Implicit Neural Representations
authors: Jonathan Richard Schwarz; Jihoon Tack; Yee Whye Teh; Jaeho Lee; Jinwoo Shin
finding: Learns compact function modulations/subnetwork selection and explicitly optimizes a rate-distortion objective, including audio experiments.
proposed_application: A later-stage reference for charging function-description costs and separating shared from signal-specific information.
limitation: This is a shared-INR compression system; it does not answer our current explicit per-IMF formula-discovery question.

group: E. Joint optimization and economical learned decompositions
title: Fully learnable deep wavelet transform for unsupervised monitoring of high-frequency time series
authors: Gabriel Michau; Gaetan Frusque; Olga Fink
finding: Learns wavelet filters and thresholds while incorporating structured filter-bank properties and sparse representations.
proposed_application: A learned decomposition alternative and a model for testing constrained versus unconstrained filter learning.
limitation: Monitoring and classification results do not demonstrate low-rate speech or symbolic mode descriptions.

group: E. Joint optimization and economical learned decompositions
title: Efficient and Modular Implicit Differentiation
authors: Mathieu Blondel et al.
finding: Differentiates solutions of optimization problems through their optimality conditions.
proposed_application: Investigate differentiating a converged continuous fitter inside a learned decomposition objective.
limitation: Regularity/local-solution assumptions matter; discrete expression changes cannot simply be differentiated as continuous variables.

group: E. Joint optimization and economical learned decompositions
title: LEAF: A Learnable Frontend for Audio Classification
authors: Neil Zeghidour; Olivier Teboul; Félix de Chaumont Quitry; Marco Tagliasacchi
finding: Learns structured audio filtering and subsequent feature operations with few frontend parameters.
proposed_application: A constrained-filter initialization/control for learned bandwidth and center-frequency adaptation.
limitation: Magnitude pooling/compression discard information; LEAF cannot be used as a reconstruction-preserving decomposition without changes.

group: E. Joint optimization and economical learned decompositions
title: DDSP: Differentiable Digital Signal Processing
authors: Jesse Engel; Lamtharn Hantrakul; Chenjie Gu; Adam Roberts
finding: Integrates structured audio synthesis operations into neural training.
proposed_application: A methodological precedent for supervising the actual waveform produced by fitted parameters.
limitation: A fixed DSP synthesis structure is not unrestricted function generation or VMD.

group: E. Joint optimization and economical learned decompositions
title: Learning Sparse Neural Networks through L_0 Regularization
authors: Christos Louizos; Max Welling; Diederik P. Kingma
finding: Uses hard-concrete stochastic gates to learn exact zeros with differentiable expected sparsity penalties.
proposed_application: Adapt the gating mechanism to active modes, knots or expression terms instead of allocating the same budget to all modes.
limitation: Expected nonzero counts are a training surrogate; verify realized parameter and structure counts after selection.

group: F. Direct speech/audio parameter-coding precedents
title: Audio coding via EMD
authors: Abdel-Ouahab Boudraa; Kais Khaldi; Thierry Chonavel; Mounia Turki Hadj-Alouane; Ali Komaty
finding: Encodes local extrema of frame-wise EMD modes and incorporates a psychoacoustic model.
proposed_application: A direct baseline for sparse mode descriptions and perceptually allocated detail.
limitation: Extrema coding differs from generated analytic expressions and does not establish a learned VMD objective.

group: F. Direct speech/audio parameter-coding precedents
title: HHT-based audio coding
authors: Kais Khaldi; Abdel-Ouahab Boudraa; Bruno Torrésani; Thierry Chonavel
finding: Codes Hilbert-derived instantaneous amplitude/frequency information from EMD modes, using compact parametric modeling.
proposed_application: The close historical precedent for describing modes through their modulation trajectories.
limitation: Does not establish our joint learned-VMD plus generated-expression setup; inspect its signal classes and rate accounting.
year_note: Final volume/issue 2015; online first 2013. Author manuscript: https://hal.science/hal-00818033

group: F. Direct speech/audio parameter-coding precedents
title: Perceptual Long-Term Variable-Rate Sinusoidal Modeling of Speech
venue: IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing
authors: Laurent Girin; Mohammad Firouzmand; Sylvain Marchand
finding: Fits amplitude/phase trajectories of voiced-speech partials with perceptual criteria and variable-rate descriptions.
proposed_application: A strong reference for fitting modulation trajectories and allocating error by perceptual relevance.
limitation: Voiced sinusoidal partials and long sections differ from arbitrary 40 ms VMD modes.
evidence: Author-hosted abstract and analysis/synthesis introduction inspected

group: G. Evaluation and survey entry points
title: MAPSS: Manifold-based Assessment of Perceptual Source Separation
authors: Amir Ivry; Samuele Cornell; Shinji Watanabe
finding: Separates perceptual leakage and self-distortion using learned representations and manifold-based measures.
proposed_application: Consider for later full-speech evaluation; first verify applicability beyond source separation.
limitation: High frame-rate outputs do not establish validity on an isolated 40 ms IMF; do not replace current fit diagnostics with it.

group: G. Evaluation and survey entry points
title: Recent Advances in Symbolic Regression
authors: Junlan Dong; Jinghui Zhong
finding: Reviews symbolic-regression methods, algorithmic developments and evaluation issues.
proposed_application: A broad reading map for extending the generator/search baseline.
limitation: Survey-level evidence; verify individual technical claims against the original papers.

group: G. Evaluation and survey entry points
title: A review of differentiable digital signal processing for music and speech synthesis
authors: Ben Hayes; Jordie Shier; György Fazekas; Andrew McPherson; Charalampos Saitis
finding: Reviews differentiable audio synthesis, optimization pathologies and practical synthesis structures.
proposed_application: A useful guide to choosing differentiable oscillatory and source-filter components.
limitation: A survey, not an experimental demonstration of our architecture.

group: H. Relevant preprints; not verified published papers
title: Robust Spatiotemporal Forecasting Using Adaptive Deep-Unfolded Variational Mode Decomposition
authors: Osama Ahmad; Lukas Wesemann; Fabian Waschkowski; Zubair Khalid
finding: Unrolls VMD updates and learns mode-specific bandwidth parameters and a complex multiplier; presents a two-stage traffic-forecasting pipeline.
proposed_application: The closest found explicit neural-VMD implementation to inspect when designing a differentiable VMD block.
limitation: ArXiv says under review; no peer-reviewed acceptance verified. Its objective and evaluation are not speech compression.
evidence: Author-preprint method equations and two-stage architecture description inspected

group: H. Relevant preprints; not verified published papers
title: Symbolic Regression with Multimodal Large Language Models and Kolmogorov Arnold Networks
authors: Thomas R. Harvey; Fabian Ruehle; Kit Fraser-Taliente; James Halverson
finding: Proposes expressions from function plots, numerically fits constants, evolves candidates and can symbolify learned KAN edge functions.
proposed_application: A direct function-proposal alternative that may use a much broader implicit mathematical vocabulary.
limitation: No publication acceptance verified; LLM priors, API costs and reproducibility require separate evaluation. It does not guarantee an unconstrained optimum.
evidence: Author-preprint proposal, numerical optimization and genetic-loop sections inspected
